notifications.bell.emptyTitle: Shown when there are no notifications.
notifications.bell.goToSet: Button on an urgent notification opening the called set.
notifications.bell.groupSummary: Summary of a group of notifications. {latest} is the newest one's title, in lower case.
notifications.bell.happeningNow: Heading over urgent notifications, such as a set called to a station.
notifications.bell.label: The notification bell's name, and the heading of its panel.
notifications.category.account: Push notification setting: notices about the reader's own account.
notifications.category.account.descripti: Under the Your account setting. Premium is the paid cosmetic upgrade, bought as a block of time that does not renew.
notifications.category.announcement: Push notification setting: messages from organisers.
notifications.category.claimResolved: Push notification setting: a player claim is decided.
notifications.category.doublesInvite: Push notification setting: a doubles partner request.
notifications.category.eventTransfer: Push notification setting: an event moving between communities.
notifications.category.gameRequest: Push notification setting: a requested game is decided.
notifications.category.roleGranted: Push notification setting: being given a role.
notifications.category.roleGranted.descr: Under the Roles & invites setting. TO is a tournament organiser.
notifications.category.setCalled: Push notification setting: your set is called to a station.
notifications.category.setCalled.descrip: Under the Set called setting. TO is a tournament organiser.
notifications.category.setReady: Push notification setting: your next set is ready to play.
notifications.discord.checkInOpen: Posted once in a community's Discord channel when an online tournament opens check-in, with a Check in button under it. Entrants confirm they are present, or they are dropped from the bracket when it starts.
notifications.discord.checkInOpen.waitin: The line under the check-in announcement in Discord. {players} is a list of the entrants who have not checked in yet, as Discord mentions.
notifications.discord.flip: The label of a button under a set's call in a community's Discord channel. Pressing it flips a coin for who hosts the set, or who is player one, and posts who won the flip.
notifications.email.footer: The last paragraph of every email Dizzy sends about a person's account. It says the email is a message about their account, never marketing, and that they can answer it.
notifications.email.moderation.appealLin: A line near the end of an email about a moderator's decision. {url} is the full web address of the form that appeals the decision.
notifications.email.moderation.closed: The subject and first line of the email sent when a site moderator closed (deleted) the person's account for breaking the Terms. There is no notice on Dizzy for this, because the account no longer exists.
notifications.email.moderation.closedBod: The line after the subject in the email about a closed account: what closing it did.
notifications.push.checkInOpen: A tournament the recipient entered has opened check-in: they confirm they are present before it starts, or they are dropped from the bracket.
notifications.push.claim.approved: A player profile the recipient said was theirs has been confirmed as theirs, so its past results now count as the recipient's.
notifications.push.complaint.notUpheld: Notification that a moderator looked at someone's complaint or appeal and decided Dizzy had not got it wrong. {reference} is the complaint's reference.
notifications.push.complaint.note: Second line of a complaint outcome notice. {note} is the moderator's own words explaining the decision, in whatever language they wrote them.
notifications.push.complaint.received: Notification confirming Dizzy received a complaint or appeal someone made while signed in. {reference} is the complaint's reference, like C-7KQ2XM.
notifications.push.complaint.receivedBod: Second line of the notification confirming a complaint arrived.
notifications.push.complaint.receivedInt: Second line of the notification confirming a complaint arrived, when the complaint is about an intimate image shared without consent. Those are dealt with first.
notifications.push.complaint.upheld: Notification that a moderator agreed with someone's complaint or appeal, so Dizzy undoes what it can. {reference} is the complaint's reference.
notifications.push.doubles.dropped: Doubles: a tournament organiser removed the recipient from the bracket because they had no partner when it was set up.
notifications.push.doubles.invited: Doubles: another player ({player}) asked the recipient to be their partner in a two-player team.
notifications.push.doubles.restored: Doubles: a tournament organiser put the recipient back into the bracket after dropping them.
{reason} is the staff member's own short explanation, in whatever language they wrote it.
notifications.push.gameRequest.filed: For site staff: people importing tournaments asked for a game that Dizzy doesn't list yet. n is how many asked.
notifications.push.matchFound.by: Push title when a ladder pairs the player with an opponent: they must press Ready by this time or lose their place. {time} is a clock time, e.g. 20:14. The opponent is deliberately not named.
notifications.push.matchFound.within: The same push for someone with no time zone saved, so the deadline is given as minutes from now instead of a clock time.
notifications.push.moderation.announceme: Notification to the person who sent an event announcement, when a site moderator removed it for breaking the Terms. {title} is the announcement's title, {event} the event's name.
notifications.push.moderation.appeal: The second line of every notice about a moderator's decision. {reason} is the moderator's own words, in whatever language they wrote them. {path} is the address of the form that appeals this decision, like /complaints/appeal/D-7KQ2PXMA.
notifications.push.moderation.capabiliti: Notification that a site moderator gave or took away staff permissions on the person's account.
notifications.push.moderation.claimRevok: Notification that a site moderator unlinked the person's account from a player profile they had claimed. {player} is the player's name.
notifications.push.moderation.communityR: Notification that a site moderator took away the person's moderator role in a community. {community} is its name.
notifications.push.moderation.eventDelet: Notification to an event's hosts that a site moderator deleted it. {event} is its name.
notifications.push.moderation.eventRoleR: Notification that a site moderator took away the person's role (such as organiser) at an event. {event} is its name.
notifications.push.moderation.imageTaken: Notification to the person who uploaded a picture, when a site moderator took it down everywhere on Dizzy. {basis} is why: someone's copyright, the law, or Dizzy's rules.
notifications.push.moderation.playerBann: Notification that a site moderator banned the person's player profile: its name shows as Banned everywhere. {player} is the player's name.
notifications.push.moderation.playerDeta: Notification that a site moderator edited the person's player profile. {player} is the player's name after the change.
notifications.push.moderation.playerUnba: Notification that a site moderator lifted a player ban. {player} is the player's name.
notifications.push.moderation.premiumDay: Notification to a person whose Premium (the paid extra that changes how their player looks) a site moderator lengthened, for example to make up for an outage or a perk taken away.
notifications.push.moderation.premiumRef: Notification to a person who asked for their money back within 14 days of buying Premium: a site moderator refunded the whole purchase, to the bank card it was paid with.
notifications.push.moderation.premiumTim: Notification to a person who lost some Premium time (a perk was taken away, or the site was down for more than a day) and chose money instead of the time: a site moderator refunded that part, to the bank card it was paid with.
notifications.push.moderation.reinstated: Notification that a site moderator lifted a suspension: the person can sign in again.
notifications.push.moderation.replayTake: Notification to the person who uploaded a replay (the recording of one game in a set), when a site moderator took it down.
notifications.push.moderation.resultCorr: Notification to the players in a set that a site moderator changed its recorded result. {tournament} is the tournament's name.
notifications.push.moderation.suspended: Notification that a site moderator suspended the person's account: they cannot sign in until it is lifted.
notifications.push.moderation.tournament: Notification to an event's hosts that a site moderator deleted one of its tournaments. {tournament} is the tournament's name, {event} the event's.
notifications.push.moderation.under18Fla: Notification that a site moderator removed an under-18 mark. {player} is the player's name.
Notification that a site moderator marked the person's player profile as belonging to someone under 18, which hides some of it. {player} is the player's name.
notifications.push.moderation.warned: Notification that a site moderator gave the person a warning. Nothing else about the account changed.
notifications.push.moderation.why: The second line of a notice about a moderator's decision in the person's favour, such as a suspension lifted. {reason} is the moderator's own words.
notifications.push.nameHold.held: Notification to the account that claims a player record: a moderator has hidden the record (its name reads as a placeholder everywhere) while a privacy request about it is decided. {player} is the record's real name.
notifications.push.nameHold.lifted: Notification to the account that claims a player record: the privacy request is decided and the record is no longer hidden. {player} is the record's real name.
notifications.push.premium.ended: Notification when the Premium time the reader bought has run out. Nothing is taken away: the handle stays, the uploaded profile picture is hidden until they buy more.
notifications.push.premium.ending: Notification a week before the Premium time the reader bought runs out. {days} is the whole days left.
notifications.push.report.actioned: Notification to someone who reported content on Dizzy, when a moderator acted on the report (took something down, banned a player, and so on). {reference} is the report's reference, like R-7KQ2XM.
notifications.push.report.dismissed: Notification to someone who reported content on Dizzy, when a moderator decided nothing needed to change. {reference} is the report's reference.
notifications.push.report.note: The second line of a report outcome notice. {note} is the moderator's own words to the reporter, in whatever language they wrote them.
notifications.push.role.event: The recipient was given a role at an event. host, to, captain and streamer are the four roles; TO means tournament organiser. {event} is the event's name.
notifications.push.role.seriesRunner: The recipient may now run events in a series (a recurring run of events under one name).
notifications.push.setCalled.station: A tournament organiser has sent the player's set to a station (a setup: console, screen, controllers) to play now. {station} is its name.
notifications.push.setReady: Push and bell title: the player's next set has both players and will be called soon. {tournament} is the tournament's name.
notifications.push.setReady.vs: As setReady, naming the opponent ({opponent}, a player or team name). vs is the usual gaming abbreviation for versus.
notifications.push.slurCheck.addressSwap: Notification when Dizzy made a page's web address from letters and numbers, because the name it would have used matched the short list of slurs Dizzy blocks. {name} is the name the person typed.
Second line of that notification. {path} is the complaints form's address, /complaints.
notifications.push.stageStarted.later.se: A later stage of a tournament (pools, then a top bracket) has begun. {stage} is the stage's name; n is how many sets this player has in it.
notifications.push.stageStarted.nextStag: Stands in for {stage} in the stageStarted.later lines when the stage has no name, so it starts a sentence.
notifications.push.transfer.offered: Another community offered to hand one of its events over to the recipient's community.
notifications.push.transfer.orphanClaim: For site staff: someone asked to take over an event that no community owns.
